shortDescription: Stacks up to 7 playable z-levels (3 up / 3 down) into ONE banded RimWorld Map joined by synthetic RegionLink wormholes, so hauling, needs, work and storage come free from vanilla. Four vanilla-matched per-level sizes (126/190/250/300) and level counts are bought from a fixed 192,000-cell budget. Per-colony climate bands make high levels genuinely alpine. Content on lower levels draws smaller once per level of drop, which is what makes a deep column read as depth.
body:
> **NOTE TO SELF:** running spec, not a changelog. §1-19 architecture; §20 compat library; §21-22 OPEN BUGS. Keep every ⚠ - each cost a run to learn.

# As above, So below II (V2)

> V1 is DELETED. ~72 files, ~20,500 LOC. No em-dashes anywhere in shipped text.

## Pitch
Up to seven z-levels in ONE RimWorld `Map`. Priorities: (1) visual clarity from above, (2) performance, (3) vanilla parity.

## Status
Visuality, QOL, altitude/weather, settings VERIFIED IN PLAY.
**#231: the 250 tier is VERIFIED IN PLAY** - `map (250, 1, 768), bands=3, slot=256`, exactly 192,000 cells, clean (§2).
UNVERIFIED: below-snow, depth shrink (§6g), camera anchor (§8a), the §18 audit, reroll grid, VEE compat (§20b 1-2), GL roof fix (§20b 4), tiers 126/190/300.

**⚠ THREE BUGS FROM THE PUBLISHED BUILD.**
1. Preview only worked at 190x190 - **FIXED** (§6d-CLAMP).
2. Fog/rocks regenerate on save reload - **NOT DIAGNOSED, HELD** (§21).
3. GL installed -> no rivers - **MECHANISM NOW IDENTIFIED AND PARTLY OURS** (§22).

---

# 1. ARCHITECTURE
One `Map`, size `(w, 1, bandCount * Slot)`. Bands stack along +z from the deepest basement, gutter between them. `Slot = ceil((bandHeight + MinGutter)/64)*64`; **64-alignment of SLOT is load-bearing** (terrain shaders sample by world position). Sizes 126/190/250/300.

**The one insight.** `Region.Neighbors` is *topological, not spatial*. Wormhole `RegionLink`s between one-cell `RegionType.Portal` ends conduct connectivity without merging rooms, temperature or vacuum, and `Reachability.CanReach` works unpatched. But reachability is not a path: 1.6's pathfinder is jobified and cannot traverse a synthetic link, hence segmented movement (§3).

**Hard 1.6 constraints.** Path grid is an IJobParallelFor over EVERY cell, so total stacked cells is the runtime metric. No `PathFinder.FindPath`. `BlocksDiagonalMovement` trips on unwalkable cells.

**⚠ The stack is 2x to 7x anisotropic.** Anything vanilla normalises by BOTH map dimensions is distorted - a bug class that cannot appear on an ordinary square map.

### ⚠ THE SLICING RULE, six shapes
| Shape | Example | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Anchor, a point as a fraction of `Size.z` | river/lake centre; random/edge cell (§15a); VEE Crater jitter | remap the point |
| Field, a gradient centred on map centre | coastline (§6e); VEE LoneIsland and Crater | re-centre the sample coordinate |
| Noise space, a slice is not a short map | Map Preview (§6d); **GL landform grids (§22)** | generate at full height, then crop |
| Distance-to-extent, a margin off `Size` | `CloseToEdge`, no-build edge; river WIDTH | re-base onto the cell's band rect |
| **Aspect ratio, normalised by BOTH dims** | preview window and reroll grid (§6d) | lay out from the BAND, generate at the STACK |
| **Map-wide scalar** | snow melt (§7), temperature readout (§16), GL roof sweep | rewrite it per cell at the consumer |

**⚠ A SEVENTH SHAPE, discovered by §22: FOREIGN ABSOLUTE WRITES.** A third-party generator that writes to absolute map coordinates lands wherever its own arithmetic puts it - which on a banded map is usually band 0 - and is then subject to whatever our carve does to that band. Neither side is individually wrong. See §22.

Still unaudited: Basin, Cavern, Chasm, Cliffs, Hollow, Valley (all `FalloffAtAngle`).

**`ABBandLocal.cs` is THE canonical FIELD rewrite** plus `BandLocalModule`, a `ModuleBase` wrapper for consumers that sample a noise field directly.

# 2. LEVEL PLAN, budget 192,000 cells

## ⚠ THE 64 CONSTRAINT IS ON *SLOT*, NOT ON BAND HEIGHT
The original tiers were all 64k-2 - the *tightest* fit - and **that coincidence was mistaken for the requirement for months**.

| size | slot | gutter | cells/band | playable | max levels | total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 126 | 128 | 2 | 16,128 | 98.4% | 7 (cap) | 112,896 |
| 190 | 192 | 2 | 36,480 | 99.0% | 5 | 182,400 |
| **250** | 256 | 6 | 64,000 | 97.7% | 3 | **192,000** ✅ VERIFIED #231 |
| **300** | 320 | 20 | 96,000 | 93.8% | 2 | **192,000** |

**Budget is tuned:** 192,000 is simultaneously `3 x 64,000` and `2 x 96,000`; `6 x 190`, `4 x 250`, `3 x 300` refused. Ladder 7/5/3/2, monotone, every tier yields real z-levels - which is why 350/382 are not offered.

**⚠ 200 IS THE ONE NUMBER TO AVOID** - just past the 192 boundary: slot 256, gutter 56, 21.9% wasted. **Waste is a SAWTOOTH.**
**⚠ A WIDE GUTTER IS A FEATURE** - "a spatial helper that reaches 22 rows will cross a 2-row gutter" is the root of §15a and §4.
**Old saves are safe.** `bandHeight` is scribed per map; `SlotFor` is generic.
Per-level size is SQUARE, so `CountFromPer10kCells` already yields a per-BAND count. **`Size.x == bandHeight` is a repair tool.**

**⚠ THE PLAN PERSISTS BETWEEN COLONIES AND SILENTLY CONSTRAINS THE SIZE.** #231's first map generated `7 bands of 126 | 3 up / 3 down` when 250/3 was intended. Nothing broken - at 7 levels 250 costs 448,000 against 192,000, so it is correctly greyed out. **Reduce levels BEFORE the larger size is selectable.** Read the PLAN line before believing any size test.

**⚠ Own the widget, do not patch the data.** `MapSizes` is `static readonly` and the reflection swap SILENTLY FAILED. Our radio buttons write `GameInitData.mapSize` directly - **the authoritative record of the player's choice (§6d-CLAMP).** **Adding a tier means growing the `InitialSize` postfix** (now +288f).
**⚠ The chooser LATCHES global state, released in a `Finalizer`** (§18a).

# 3. CROSS-BAND MOVEMENT
Segmented at ONE interception: `StartPath` prefix, tick sweep, `Carry` re-issues `StartPath`. `ABWormhole.TryGetTransit` BFSes the band graph; hops must strictly decrease. **Multi-hop routing UNTESTED IN PLAY.**

# 4. GROUP ORDERING
`RecomputeDestinations` spreads the selection along the drag line, which between bands runs through the GUTTER. The odd/even signature ("3 and 5 fail, 2 and 4 do not") is the proof: only ODD counts sample exactly 0.5. Verified.

# 5. ⚠ ONE DESCENT RULE: `ABBands.TryResolveVisibleBelow`
Descends while each level is see-through, stops at the first opaque floor. TEN systems share it. **EIGHT appearances of the single `- Slot` bug** (the eighth as INDEX arithmetic, invisible to the standing `grep '- Slot'` audit).
**`TryResolveVisibleFrom` is THE gate.** Two legitimate exceptions: `SectionLayer_ABBelowV2` needs "in bounds but fogged"; upward-shape consumers ask a different question.

# 6. SKY-MASS PRESENTATION (verified)
Despeckle (walls dissolve only at 7+ open neighbours; at 6 it ate the outermost wall row off every meadow edge), one central fog hole, five-terrain plateau palette, cliff faces, alpine pass.
**⚠ The mass tapers with altitude, so +3 may contain NO LAND AT ALL.**
Ore glyph bug: ore defs have no `naturalTerrain`, so a "can't happen" fallback drew the whole atlas sheet per cell.

# 6a. ⚠ THE BELOW VIEW IS MIRRORED PASSES, NOT ONE RENDERER
`SectionLayer_ABBelowV2` ports vanilla `SectionLayer_Terrain` **and nothing else**. Confirmed twice: Water (§6b), Snow (§6f).
**⚠ THE CONVERSE IS HANDLED.** A foreign `Thing.Print` postfix prints into OUR layer and is still correct, because the call is bracketed `SnapshotVertCounts()` -> `Print` -> `FinishNewVerts` and **`FinishNewVerts` transforms by VERTEX RANGE**. Preserve that.
**Ascent rule:** the dirty mirror stops at the first opaque floor, tested over the cell and its eight neighbours; the FIRST step stays unconditional (MountainCap). Mirrors vanilla's `ProgramState` guard.
**⚠ THE UNIT OF WASTE IS A SECTION REGENERATION, NOT A CELL.**

# 6b. ⚠ WATER: a TWO-PASS SCREEN-SPACE effect
The visible `Map/TerrainWater` samples the WaterDepth subcamera's texture at its own SCREEN position. `SectionLayer_ABBelowWatergen` targets `SubcameraDefOf.WaterDepth.LayerId`.
Rivers: remap `GetRiverCenter` (not `Init`, which consumes it immediately); `GetLakeCenter` needs the same patch or it undoes the first. Width clamped at the producer.
**⚠ ALL THREE ARE INERT WHEN GL IS INSTALLED - CONFIRMED (`riverGraph: 0 node(s)`), §22.**

# 6c. DUBS MINT MINIMAP (verified)
ONE RECT. `DrawTextureFitted` preserves the TEXTURE's aspect, so use `ScaleMode.StretchToFill`.

# 6d. MAP PREVIEW
Builds a bare Map on a background thread, so our banding prefix never fires. **Generate at full stacked height, crop via `TexCoords`.** `MaxMapSize.z` MUST rise.

## 6d-CLAMP. ⚠ PUBLISHED BUG: PREVIEW ONLY WORKED AT 190x190 (FIXED)
`Stacked()` ran the incoming size through `Clamp()`, which returns *the largest offered size ≤ input that fits at the current level count*. Map Preview passes VANILLA's size (250 default):
```
Clamp(250) at 4 levels -> 190  ->  lastBandHeight = 190
TryBandRows: BandCount * SlotFor(190) == stackedZ ?  only true if 190 was chosen
```
**Fix: `PlannedSize`.** `Clamp` is LOSSY by design and was answering "what did the player choose?" - never a derivation problem, since the chooser writes `mapSize` directly. Also fixed: `Stacked` clamped x and z INDEPENDENTLY though a band is square; `FixWindowAspect` re-Clamped.

**⚠ MAP PREVIEW SHIPS IN TWO HALVES, AND GL BUNDLES ONE.** Engine half byte-identical in both; `MapPreviewWindow`/`MapSeedRerollWindow` live ONLY in `MapPreviewMod.dll`. **With GL installed and Map Preview absent, `Active` is TRUE while window types are ABSENT.** Safe only because every target is null-guarded independently. **Do not "simplify" `Active`.**

## 6d-REROLL (UNVERIFIED)
**⚠ Opened COMPLETELY EMPTY:** `elementSize.y = 403/126*896 = 2,866 px` -> `gridSize.y = 0` -> `DesiredCount = 0`. **The SECOND consumer of the stacked size caught out by it.** Fixed by a postfix re-deriving from BAND height - repairing two statics, not reimplementing.

# 6e. COASTS (verified)
CENTRED wrong, not scaled wrong. NO SCALING. **⚠ "None override `GetNoiseValue`" is about VANILLA ONLY** - VEE's LoneIsland declares its own and drowns the colony.

# 6f. BELOW-SNOW (UNVERIFIED)
**No mirror of `SectionLayer_Snow` existed.** Near-miss: `CellTerrainAt` samples `snowGrid.GetDepth(below)` correctly, but it is consumed only by `MaterialFor` to pick the POLLUTED variant.
Geometry built once (NOT `ClearSubMeshes(All)`); iteration order must match `MakeBaseGeometry`; empty cells still emit nine transparent vertices. **⚠ Queue-decided draw order may need work.**

# 6g. DEPTH SHRINK (UNVERIFIED)
- **⚠ The atlas trap:** past `ZoomRootSize` 18 humanlikes render from a cached atlas blit ignoring `PawnDrawParms.matrix`. **Verify across that boundary both ways.**
- Right-multiply the pawn matrix; a left multiply slides below pawns toward the origin.
- **⚠ Exclusions kept verbatim:** LINKED graphics print one quad per cell; natural rock excluded BY DEF, because Better Mountains swaps rock to non-linked `Graphic_Random`.
- **ReGrowth does NOT contest this.**
**⚠ PERSPECTIVE MODE WAS BUILT AND REMOVED. Do not re-add as polish.**

# 7. PER-LEVEL CHARACTER
Ore `x(1+0.45*(depth-1))`, caves `x(1+0.35*(depth-1))`, after the clamp. **Ore scales `basementOreDensity` through our OWN `ABOreGen.ScatterOres`.**
**⚠ The snow line never worked, and the comment saying it did not need to was wrong.**

# 8. CAMERA
**The clamp and level-switch input share `ABGuard.Camera`**, both per-frame paths where an unthrottled `Log.Error` turns a cosmetic bug into a hang.

# 8a. NEW-GAME CAMERA ANCHOR (UNVERIFIED)
Two things move the colony AFTER `PlayerStartSpot`: `RescueStrandedColonists` and the carve. **Only `StartedNewGame` runs after vanilla's own camera jump.**
**⚠ OPEN:** `z=24` was EXACTLY `PodScatterMargin`; vanilla's pick and my clamp look identical from outside.

# 9. GENERATION COST

## 9a. The profile stamps its own conditions
`ABGenProfile.Report` prints `TILE`, `PLAN`, `SCOPING:`, two censuses. Has now voided or explained five comparisons.
**⚠ THE WATER REPORT DOES NOT DO THIS AND SHOULD.** #231's water report gave a clean answer for a map whose TILE, MUTATORS and PLAN it never printed. **Add TILE + mutators + PLAN + surfaceBand emphasis to `ABWaterBand.Report`.**

## 9b. ⚠ "COST IS DESTRUCTION NOT GENERATION" - NO LONGER TRUE, AND THE FIX IS WHY
#188: gensteps 3,972 ms, carve 20,447 ms, 74,584 destroyed (16/84).
**#231 INVERTS IT: gensteps 3,836 ms (71%), carve 1,580 ms (29%), 4,575 destroyed.** Rock suppression worked, so the carve got cheap and cost moved to generation. **16/84 is a historical record of a fixed problem, not a current fact.**

## 9c-9e. Rock, and the basement
#190 census: 43,517 rock SUPPRESSED vs 4,939 DESTROYED. `ABDoomedBands` suppresses `GenSpawn.Spawn(ThingDef,...)` in sky bands - safe by **shape**, **state-neutrality**, **sky only**.
Basement FillRock is the remaining carve cost (926 of 1,580 ms in #231). **⚠ My own §9d caution was falsified:** the basement keep hits only 14.4%; suppressing trades 7,113 destroys (~1.4 s) for 6,873 spawns (~200 ms), net ~1.2 s.
**Sign flip, a confirmation not a bug:** with rock suppressed `Sky clear` INVERTED (rising with altitude) because rock tapers upward, so higher bands have more OPEN ground and chunks only grow on open ground.

## 9f. ⚠ EVERY ABSOLUTE TIMING PREDATES THE TIER CHANGE
3 x 250 is 192,000 cells vs 7 x 126's 112,896 - 1.7x. Re-baseline before comparing across it.

## 9g. ⚠ NEW #1 CANDIDATE: `GenStep_Plants` IN DOOMED BANDS
#231, `7 x 126` TropicalSwamp: **`GenStep - Plants 2270.1 ms` = 59% of ALL genstep time.** Six of seven bands doomed (95,256 of 112,896 cells), so **~84% is vegetation grown then erased**. Same shape §9d solves for rock.
**⚠ n=1, ON THE HIGHEST-PLANT-DENSITY BIOME IN THE GAME.** Mechanism tile-independent, magnitude not. Confirm on a second biome first.
### Ranked
1. `GenStep_Plants` doomed-band suppression (~1.9 s on #231's tile).
2. Basement rock suppression (~1.2 s).
3. `GenStep_RockChunks` - `Filth_RubbleRock` still top destroyed def in #231 (2,462 of 4,575).
4. Scattered ruins (also a CONTENT BUG - surface loses ruins vanilla intended).
5. `ABRockGen.PickIndex` Perlin precompute. NOT DONE: changes determinism.

# 10, 11. PERF
59.6 fps at 96 pawns. **⚠ THAT BENCHMARK MEASURES THE WRONG THING** - cost is in section-regeneration BURSTS. Perf claims need a mining/construction test with a multi-level plan.

# 12. DIAGNOSTICS
**⚠ Bisect toggles PERSIST across runs.** #172 opened with a stale `belowWater=False` that mimicked a fixed bug exactly. Now STAMPED INTO THE PROFILE.
**⚠ Poll the monitor even when nothing auto-prompts.**
**⚠ The pre-pinned palette always strips its LAST entry.** **n=4** - #231 lost the deliberate `camera calibration` padding and kept all three real instruments. **Keep padding with a DISTINCT throwaway.**
**⚠ THE AUTO-PROMPT IS EDGE-TRIGGERED, SO CHECK THE COUNT, NOT THE TEXT.** In #231 a second water-report click produced no prompt (same stack signature). `monitor_get_error` returned the LATEST occurrence - which was still the FIRST one, byte-identical and stale. **`count` is the only way to tell a fresh reading from an old one.** Nearly analysed stale data as new.
**⚠ Debug actions are `AllowedGameStates.PlayingOnMap`.** They silently do nothing on the world map / preview screen. "I clicked it" plus no count change means the player was not on a map yet.

# 13. OPEN WORK
1. **§22 GL landforms** - decide the interception. Now the highest-value bug: it likely disables ALL GL landform shaping on any map with a basement, not just rivers.
2. **§21 fog/rocks on reload** - the two-question observation.
3. **§9g plants** - confirm on a second biome, then implement.
4. Verify tiers 126/190/300; preview fix explicitly at 300.
5. Verify §18 audit, VEE compat, GL roof fix, reroll grid, depth shrink, camera anchor, below-snow.
6. Stamp TILE/PLAN into the water report (§9a).
7. Basement rock suppression; §9g 4-5; audit the other `FalloffAtAngle` mutators.
8. **Never exercised:** multi-hop stair router, elevator, basement PATHING/wormholes, cavern basement.
9. Below-pawn drawing serial and cache-disabled; realtime-things pass single-band and unshrunk.
10. `ShotReport` drops target size. Biomes! at 40%. **Store page still says three levels.**

# 14. LESSONS
**Method.** Prove a subsystem innocent by finding a state where the suspect CANNOT EXIST. Re-open a rejection only by naming the confound. Change one thing per experiment. Run the diagnostic before the third theory. A beautiful fit is not evidence.
**⚠ CHECK THAT YOUR CONFIGURATION CAN EXPRESS THE DIFFERENCE BEFORE RUNNING THE EXPERIMENT.** #231's water report was clean and **worthless as a discriminator**: with `0 down / 2 up`, `surfaceBand = 0`, so "the river lands in band 0" and "the river lands on the surface" are THE SAME SENTENCE. **Write down what each hypothesis predicts for THIS setup first; if the predictions match, change the setup.**
**⚠ THE CONFIGURATION THAT HIDES A BUG IS ALSO THE ONE THAT REVEALS ITS MECHANISM.** The same variable (`surfaceBand`) that made #231 undiscriminating turned out to BE the mechanism - band 0 is the surface when there is no basement, and a doomed rock-filled band when there is. A useless experiment and the answer differed by one setting.
**⚠ Measure the ratio before optimising the half you assumed - and RE-measure after you fix it.** Generation was 16% and is now 71% (§9b) *because the fix worked*. A ratio is a snapshot, not a property.
**⚠ Stamp the experiment's conditions into its own output** - and **apply it to EVERY diagnostic, not just the one that taught you**.
**⚠ Evidence consistent with both hypotheses is not evidence.**
**⚠ THE SYMPTOM SET IS ITSELF EVIDENCE - ask what the affected things SHARE.** §21 named fog AND rocks and nothing else: precisely the two things stored as flat per-cell arrays sized by `map.Area`.
**⚠ CHECK THE OCCURRENCE COUNT BEFORE TRUSTING A RE-READ.** Edge-triggered reporting returns the latest occurrence, which may be the original.
**⚠ Aim at the fact, not the record of the intent.** `GameInitData.mapSize` IS the player's choice.
**⚠ A LOSSY NORMALISER IS NOT A WAY TO READ A CHOICE.** When a function's contract is "snap to something valid", it can never RECOVER a value.
**⚠ A CONSTRAINT SATISFIED BY EVERY EXAMPLE IS NOT NECESSARILY THE CONSTRAINT.** All three original sizes were 64k-2; the real rule was only that *Slot* is 64-aligned. **Derive the constraint from the mechanism, not from what you already built.**
**⚠ THE REAL CONFLICT IS USUALLY A REPLACEMENT, NOT A COLLISION.** GL *substitutes its own worker*, so our patches never run. **A patch silently never invoked produces no error, no log line, no conflict warning.** `riverGraph: 0 node(s)` is what that looks like. **Ask what a mod REPLACES, not only what it patches.**
**⚠ AND THE BUG AFTER THAT IS USUALLY A COLLABORATION.** §22 is not GL's fault or ours: GL writes to absolute map rows (correct for a map it thinks is 250x768) and our carve overwrites those rows (correct for a basement). **Two locally-correct behaviours composing into a broken result. When neither side is wrong, look at the ORDER they run in.**
**⚠ A SHARED METHOD NAME IS A HYPOTHESIS, NOT A CONFLICT.** Name-matching false-positive rate 50%; ReGrowth cleared four times.
**⚠ Compat work is mostly deletion.** **⚠ Design for the foreign patch you have not met.** **⚠ Waste is often a sawtooth.** **⚠ The thing you rounded away may be load-bearing.** **⚠ A rule enforced by grepping a SYNTAX only catches that syntax.** **⚠ Duplication is how an invariant dies.** **⚠ A comment is not an invariant.** **⚠ Steady-state fps hides burst cost.** **⚠ Timing that reads exactly 0.0 ms is an early return.** **⚠ In a foreign log, the loudest error is usually downstream.** **⚠ A finding scoped to vanilla does not transfer to mods.**
**Patching.** Re-aim the shared parameter. Find the ONE virtual everything funnels through - and when there is none, **wrap the DATA instead of the reader**. Patch the PRODUCER, not the store. Own the widget. Never put a foreign type in a patch signature - type `__instance` as `object`. **Suppress the callee, not the caller.** **Prefix state is released in a Finalizer.** **Repair a foreign method's output rather than reimplementing it.** **Never clamp a Def field to fix one map.** **Prefer a published ExtensionPoint over racing internals.**
**Engine facts.** `holdSnowOrSand` defaults TRUE. Draw order is material render QUEUE, not altitude. `Banded` is FALSE for all of map generation. `SectionLayer` subclasses auto-discovered on EVERY map. FinalizeInit runs on a worker thread - generation latches must be `[ThreadStatic]`. Ore defs have no `naturalTerrain`. `CameraJumper.TryJump` and `MapDrawer.MapMeshDirty` return silently unless `ProgramState == Playing`. Humanlikes past `ZoomRootSize` 18 render from an atlas blit ignoring `PawnDrawParms.matrix`. **Gensteps run with live-map bookkeeping DEFERRED (~40x cheaper than after `FinalizeInit`).** Harmony skips POSTFIXES when the original throws but always runs FINALIZERS; **a prefix returning false skips the original but POSTFIXES STILL RUN**; prefix and transpiler compose. **`FogGrid` and compressible things are flat per-cell arrays sized by `map.Area`.** **`WaterInfo.GetWaterMovement` indexes `x * map.Size.z + z`.** **TileMutatorDefs compete within a `categories` entry, so a mod can REPLACE a vanilla mutator by declaring its own in the same category.** **Debug actions default to `AllowedGameStates.PlayingOnMap`.**

---

# 15-19. QOL / WEATHER / SETTINGS / AUDIT / FOREIGN MODLIST
**15a.** Nothing may exist in the void - finders answer inside the surface band; a `GenSpawn.Spawn` prefix rewrites `loc`; a 120-tick sweep catches teleports and pre-fix saves.
**15b.** `CloseToEdge` measured against `map.Size`, so the surface band reported itself as inland everywhere. One prefix re-bases onto the band rect; eleven cold call sites inherit it. **ONE surface-edge finder**; a null dir means "any side, re-rolled" deliberately.
**15d.** Vanilla's no-build edge REMOVED - consequence: that strip is also what stops a colony sealing its map edge. **15e.** Drop pods fall through the levels.
**16.** `AB_OpenAir`/`AB_WallTop` set `holdSnowOrSand=false`. Melt per band rewrites the private `outdoorMeltAmount` on EVERY call; **ReGrowth transpiles the same method and composes.** Rejected: swapping `WeatherDef.Worker.overlays`, a global Def. Readout rebuilt from `TryGetTemperatureForCell` - `OutdoorTemp` is NEVER reached because outdoor cells still belong to a Room.
**17.** **⚠ The blank-tab bug:** content height from the previous frame's `CurHeight` is a SELF-SUSTAINING LATCH without a floor. Fix `Mathf.Max(CurHeight + 16f, inner.height)`. **⚠ Draw the diagnostic OUTSIDE the thing being diagnosed.** The unlock gate writes to a LOCAL so the stored value IS the record the warning was read.
**18a.** State taken in a Prefix released in a Postfix - three instances; `ABAimAngle` swaps LIVE COMBAT STATE and opened with `patched = null`, DISCARDING a pending restore. All now `Finalizer`.
**18b.** The mirror: no `ProgramState` guard (~1.3M dead dispatches per 7-band carve), no ascent rule.
**18c.** 12 of 19 kill switches had no call site; the dev spike layout taxed every map in the game.
**18e. CLOSED:** `ABCavernGen.Generate` bails immediately without Biomes! Caverns. **Re-confirmed #231** (0.7/0.0/0.0 ms). The trap: the profile's `mutators: ... Caves` is the VANILLA TILE MUTATOR, unrelated.
**19.** 910-mod failure was **not us** - the NRE is thrown while EVALUATING ARGUMENTS to `GenerateMap`, so it is never entered. Real cause 24 lines earlier: `startingAndOptionalPawns[startingPawnCount]` with a NEGATIVE count; exactly two mods patch it.

---

# 20. COMPAT LIBRARY
**We load at #900, LAST.** Harmony precedence is by PRIORITY, not load order.

| Family | Certainty | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Grand Rivers / Epic Rivers | 98% | width clamp shipped - **inert under GL (§22)** |
| Geological Landforms | 90% | roof fix shipped (untested); **landform writes destroyed by our carve (§22)** |
| ReGrowth 2 | 80% | **cleared four times** |
| Vanilla Landmarks Expanded | 90% | 2 shipped, rest inherit or inert |
| Biomes! | 40% | least understood |
| Alpha Biomes | 50% | presumed Crater-class. **No save-path hooks - not a §21 candidate.** |

## 20b. SHIPPED (none verified in play)
1. **`Patch_VEE_LoneIsland_ABBandLocal`** - their falloff centres on `map.Center` and both passes walk `map.AllCells` writing elevation 0 + deep ocean below 0.2. On 126x896 the island is a disc of r≈76 at z=448, so **every band except the middle becomes ocean, including the surface**. One prefix on their own virtual `GetNoiseValue`.
2. **`Patch_VEE_Crater_*`** - no single sampling hook, so **wrap the three private noise fields** in `BandLocalModule`. Jitter scaled separately (`Size.z * ±0.2` is ±179 cells). ⚠ Stated cost: one property feeds both axes, so x jitter compresses too.
3. **`Patch_TileMutatorWorker_ABRiverWidth`** - clamps `RiverNode.width` to 22% of band height, at the producer, never on `RiverDef`.
4. **`Patch_GL_ABLandformRoofScope` + `Patch_RoofGrid_ABLandformSurfaceOnly`** - GL's `SetRoofsFromLandform` runs `foreach (map.AllCells) SetRoof(...)` from the SURFACE grid: ~800k calls stamping surface roofs onto every band. `[ThreadStatic]` latch released in a Finalizer + a `SetRoof` prefix.

## 20c. CLEARED - do not re-flag without a new confound
ReGrowth wall-snow (vertex range); ReGrowth `Printer_Plane` (linked graphics only, already excluded); ReGrowth `IsSaveCompressible` + `Mineable.ExposeData` (**`IsSpaceRock()`-gated - not a §21 candidate**); GL `AdjustMineables` (vanilla's field); GL priority 800 (no shared insertion point); ReGrowth `DoCellSteadyEffects`/`GetDrawParms`/`GenSpawn.Spawn`; VEE's river family and wildlife mutators.

---

# 21. ⚠ OPEN: FOG AND ROCKS ON SAVE RELOAD (HELD)
**ELIMINATED:** `ABV2.*` leakage; save compressibility; roof collapse (sky roofs ARE cleared); `RebindAfterLoad` ordering; ReGrowth (space-rock-only); Alpha Biomes / Biomes! (no save-path hooks).
**⚠ THE SYMPTOM PAIR POINTS AT US.** Fog and natural rock are exactly the two things stored as flat per-cell arrays sized by `map.Area`. Everything else - pawns, furniture, **player-built walls** - saves individually.
**Hypotheses:** (a) real data re-generated on load; (b) rendering; (c) per-cell array desync.

# 22. ⚠ GL LANDFORMS: WRITTEN INTO BAND 0, THEN DESTROYED BY OUR CARVE

## Confirmed
**GL REPLACES vanilla river generation.** `GL_River`/`GL_RiverConfluence`/etc. are `TileMutatorDef`s in the **`River` category** on `TileMutatorWorker_Landform`. Mutators compete within a category, so GL's win and vanilla's worker never runs. **#231 proved it: `riverGraph: 0 node(s)` on a `GL_RiverConfluence` tile.** Every river patch we own is therefore **inert** under GL - not conflicting, never invoked.

## The mechanism, from two runs plus a code read
**Run A - `surfaceBand=0` (0 down / 2 up), 250x768:** `band 0 water=13518, baseRiver=13115; band 1 = 0; band 2 = 0`. River present and rendering.
**Run B - a basement present (`surfaceBand>=1`):** no river anywhere. *(Player observation; the water report did NOT re-fire, so this half is UNMEASURED - see §12 on counts.)*

**Run A's own band breakdown is the key evidence.** If GL's grid spanned all 768 rows, a river would appear in bands 1 and 2 as well. It appears **only in band 0**, so GL writes to roughly map rows 0-249 - consistent with `LandformGridSize` defaulting to a square **250** and `MapSpaceToNodeSpaceFactor` entering `GridFunction.Transform<double>` as a **uniform scalar**.

**And our carve finishes it off. `FillRock`, basement bands, unconditional:**
```csharp
terrain.SetTerrain(c, rock.building?.naturalTerrain ?? TerrainDefOf.Gravel);
```
No water check, no exception - plus `ClearCellHard`. Our carve is a POSTFIX on `GenerateContentsIntoMap`, so it runs AFTER every genstep including GL's mutators.

**Chain:** GL writes the river into map rows 0-249 = band 0. With no basement, band 0 IS the surface -> river survives (Run A). With a basement, band 0 is a doomed rock-filled band -> `FillRock` overwrites the terrain -> **river erased entirely** (Run B). One mechanism, both observations, and the discriminating variable is the one that changed.

## ⚠ THE SCOPE IS MUCH LARGER THAN RIVERS
`TransformIntoMapSpace` is the funnel for **every** landform output - elevation, fertility, caves, terrain, biome grid, water flow - in both `GeneratePostElevationFertility` and `GeneratePostTerrain`. If the grid only covers band 0, then **on any banded map with a basement, ALL Geological Landforms shaping is written into the basement and then destroyed.** Landforms would do nothing at all.
**FALSIFIABLE PREDICTION, cheap to run:** a `GL_Canyon` / `GL_Crater` / `GL_Coast` tile with at least one level below the surface should generate as a *plain* map with no landform shaping. If landform shaping DOES appear on the surface, this model is wrong.

## Fix directions (undecided)
- **`TransformIntoMapSpace` is the ONE funnel** - one interception fixes every output. But it returns `IGridFunction<T>`, a foreign generic interface, so wrapping it means implementing their type (unlike `ModuleBase`, which is vanilla and subclassable). That is the design constraint to solve.
- **`GeologicalLandformsAPI.LandformGridSize`** (`ExtensionPoint<IntVec2, int>`, default 250) is published and sanctioned, and GL maintains `ModCompat_` classes. But it sets RESOLUTION, not placement, so it likely will not suffice alone.
